title: Compatibility of prescribed resolutions with the composite derived unit
statement: Let $A,B,C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] with bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-bounded-derived-subcategories]. Let $F:A\to B$ and $G:B\to C$ be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and suppose $F$ sends injective objects to $G$-acyclic objects [def-sp-composite-acyclicity]. Let $X\in A$, let $I$ be a prescribed injective resolution of $X$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and let $n\geq 0$. Put $K=F(I)$, indexed by the natural numbers, and let $L$ be its extension by zero to an integer-indexed bounded below complex. Write $Q$ for passage to the bounded below derived category, $\theta_F:H^n(RF(X[0]))\simeq R^nF(X)$ for the canonical single-object comparison [lem-sp-derived-functor-single-identification], $\iota_F:R^nF(X)\simeq H^n(K)$ and $\iota_{GF}:R^n(GF)(X)\simeq H^n(GK)$ for the resolution comparisons [lem-sp-derived-well-defined], and $b:H^n(RG(RF(X[0])))\simeq R^n(GF)(X)$ for the canonical Grothendieck abutment comparison [lem-sp-grothendieck-edge-maps]. Then there is an isomorphism $e:RF(X[0])\simeq QL$ such that $\theta_F\iota_F=H^n(e)\,\rho_L\,\epsilon_K$ and $\iota_{GF}^{-1}b^{-1}H^n(RG(e))=\epsilon_{GK}^{-1}H^n(\mu_{G,K}^{-1})\rho_{GL}^{-1}H^n(\eta_G(L))$. Here $\rho$ is the canonical comparison $H^n(QM)\simeq H^n(M)$, $\epsilon$ is the canonical homology comparison for extension by zero, $\mu_{G,K}:G(K^{\mathrm{ext}})\simeq (GK)^{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the map/extension comparison, and $\eta_G(L):Q(GL)\to RG(QL)$ is the derived unit. Composites in these equations are read from left to right. This asserts only source and ordinary-homology comparisons; there is no edge map. The two equations determine exactly the homology components used downstream. The complete transported formulas are the Lean statement below.

source.place: Tag 015M (lemma-compose-derived-functors), proof describing the canonical map on an injective resolution; Tag 015N (lemma-grothendieck-spectral-sequence), abutment identification. Canonical homology factors expanded from the resolution-identification step of lem-pc-grothendieck-hypercohomology-edge.

proof.text: Extend the prescribed injective resolution $I$ by zero. Its augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism $X[0]\to I^{\mathrm{ext}}$, so it becomes an isomorphism after $Q$. Apply $RF$ and invert its unit at $I^{\mathrm{ext}}$, which is invertible on bounded below complexes of injectives. Compose with $Q$ of the map/extension isomorphism. This explicitly constructs $e$; it is not an arbitrary object chosen from mere existence.

For the chosen injective resolution, the definition of the canonical single-object comparison gives the first equation. For the prescribed resolution, choose a comparison lifting $\mathrm{id}_X$. Comparisons of injective resolutions are homotopy equivalences; their images under additive functors induce the canonical resolution comparison on homology. Naturality of the derived unit and of the quotient-homology comparison transfers the chosen-resolution equation to $I$.

The abutment comparison uses the composition isomorphism $R(GF)\simeq RG\,RF$. Its defining right-derived uniqueness equation carries the $GF$ unit to the composite unit. Evaluate this equation at the bounded below complex of injectives $I^{\mathrm{ext}}$; the $F$ unit there is invertible. Naturality along the augmentation of $X[0]$ and cancellation of that $F$ unit leaves exactly the $G$ unit at $F(I^{\mathrm{ext}})$. This is the representative calculation in Tag 015M (lemma-compose-derived-functors), implemented by rightDerivedNatTrans_fac, rightDerivedFunctorPlusCompUnit_app, and the definition of grothendieckSpectralObjectHBotTopIso in the already proved source library.

Apply degree-$n$ homology to the last unit equation. Expand the canonical quotient-homology, map/extension and extension-homology isomorphisms. Their factors give precisely the second displayed equation. All shifts are absent from this calculation, so the same argument applies at $n=0$.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_grothendieck_resolution_unit_comparison
    {A : Type uA} [Category.{vA} A] [Abelian A] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vA} A]
    {B : Type uB} [Category.{vB} B] [Abelian B] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vB} B]
    {C : Type uC} [Category.{vC} C] [Abelian C] [IsGrothendieckAbelian.{vC} C]
    [HasDerivedCategory A] [HasDerivedCategory B] [HasDerivedCategory C]
    (F : A ⥤ B) (G : B ⥤ C) [F.Additive] [G.Additive]
    [PreservesFiniteLimits F] [PreservesFiniteLimits G]
    (hFG : (⟨F, G⟩ : GrothendieckComposablePair A B C).SendsInjectivesToAcyclics)
    (X : A) (I : InjectiveResolution X) (n : ℕ) :
    let K := (F.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj I.cocomplex
    let L : CochainComplex.Plus B := ⟨K.extend ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat, 0,
      inferInstance⟩
    ∃ e : F.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.obj
        ((DerivedCategory.Plus.singleFunctor A 0).obj X) ≅ DerivedCategory.Plus.Q.obj L,
      (F.homologyRightDerivedFunctorPlusObjSingleFunctorIso X n).hom ≫
          (I.isoRightDerivedObj F n).hom =
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor B n).map e.hom ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctorObjQIso L n).hom ≫
          (K.extendHomologyIso ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat
            (rfl : (n : ℤ) = n)).hom ∧
      (I.isoRightDerivedObj (F ⋙ G) n).inv ≫
          (F.grothendieckSpectralObjectHBotTopIso G hFG n).inv.app X ≫
          (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor C n).map
            (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlus.map e.hom) =
        (((G.mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj K).extendHomologyIso
          ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat (rfl : (n : ℤ) = n)).inv ≫
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap
          (HomologicalComplex.mapExtendIso K ComplexShape.embeddingUpNat G).inv (n : ℤ) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctorObjQIso
          (G.mapCochainComplexPlus.obj L) n).inv ≫
        (DerivedCategory.Plus.homologyFunctor C n).map
          (G.rightDerivedFunctorPlusUnit.app ((HomotopyCategory.Plus.quotient B).obj L))
